messages:
Cara: Quick sync — GCP asked for our recommended private-offer structure for Redwood Dedicated. Meeting Fri 10am PT. Thoughts on commit tiers and renewal cadence?

Jim: For sales rep motion, 12/24/36 month buckets work best. 24 gives flexibility, 36 gets better pricing. Recommend showing clear MSP uplift for 36.

Sophia: Finance prefers 12 or 36. 24 complicates revenue recognition across renewals. If we do 24, need explicit billing milestone rules.

Ravi: From solutions side — customers buying Dedicated want predictable throughput. We should tie discounts to committed GPU-hours or $ commit, not seat count. Example tiers: $50k, $150k, $500k ARR commit.

Cara: Good point. GCP expects SKU-level metering mapping though — can we map committed $ to SKU usage? @Ravi

Ravi: Yes, we can map to GPU-hour SKU + token metering for hosted add-ons. But marketplace metering has constraints (granularity, report window). See docs: https://cloud.google.com/marketplace/docs/billing/metering

Ely: Legal flags: audit rights on usage reporting, minimum notice for price changes, termination for convenience vs breach. Also want to avoid open-ended liability for partners. Need 90-day renewal notice for auto-renew? Prefer 60.

Sophia: Recommend 60 days for renewals, and allow customers to step down to a lower tier with 30-day notice but no retro refunds. That simplifies accounting.

Jim: Discount schedule proposal from GTM: 0% (no commit), 10% (mid), 20% (high), plus a 5% onboarding credit for first 3 months. Could offer additional 5% if they commit to marketplace private offer and 36-month term.

Cara: I like that. We should also define an early-termination fee (ETF) proportional to remaining committed value to discourage churn. Thoughts?

Ely: ETF is necessary. Suggest ETF = remaining committed spend * 0.5 for first half of term, 0.25 for second half. Also include data-export window and transitions.

Ravi: Technical caveat: Dedicated capacity scaling and burst policy must be honored during term. If we promise X sustained throughput and they exceed it, we either throttle or require burst billing — need clear language.

Jim: Agree. On pricing page we should show both committed rate and overage rate. Overage at 1.5x committed unit price. Clear and predictable.

Cara: Quick check — will marketplace private-offer flow allow us to embed tiered discounts + ETF? @MarketplaceBot any notes on UI constraints? :eyes:

MarketplaceBot: The Marketplace private offer APIs support per-SKU pricing and flat one-time adjustments. Complex multi-tier logic often encoded as terms in the PO + post-processing invoices. Automatable but requires mapping between PO line items and our billing system.

Sophia: That means ops work to reconcile. We should limit number of custom PO templates to 3 to stay operationally sane.

Jim: Sales feedback: Offer a renewal incentive — e.g., 5% loyalty credit on renewal if they renew >= prior commit within 30 days. Helps retention.

Ely: Watch out for anti-tying clauses in some cloud marketplaces. Can't force customers to buy both Dedicated and Support as a single bundled mandatory product. Make incentives, not mandates.

Cara: Action items: (1) @Ravi draft SKU mapping for $ commits -> GPU-hour + token add-ons, (2) @Sophia & @Ely propose billing / ETF / renewal language, (3) @Jim create 3 PO templates for Sales, (4) I'll consolidate and share with GCP ahead of Fri.

Ravi: I'll drop a mapping doc in #partnerships later today.

Sophia: I'll have revenue & accounting note by EOD.

Ely: I'll draft the legal terms and exceptions; will loop in security for data/export clauses.

Jim: I'll mock up the PO templates and sample pricing tables.

Cara: Thanks all. If anyone has customer examples (SI deals or HW partners that used similar structure), paste them here. :thumbsup: 

Ravi: We used a similar model with an on-prem hardware partner last year — will paste anonymized numbers.

MarketplaceBot: Reminder: Partner kickoff Fri 10am PT — calendar invite sent.

Cara: Perfect — see you then.
